function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.reasoning: The user typed "time". They might want to get the current time? Or they might want to run the system command "time"? In Windows, "time" is a command that sets or displays the system time. But the tool only executes commands via os.system. We could call "time" command. But maybe they want to know the current time. Let's interpret as they want to get the current time. We can use Python's datetime module. But we don't have direct code execution except via the tool. But we can just respond with the current time. Since we can't run code, we can approximate. But we can also use the tool to run a command like "echo %TIME%"? On Windows, "echo %TIME%" prints the current time. So we can call that. Use the tool: functions.cmd_controller_execute with command "echo %TIME%". That will output the time. Let's do that.
